subtitle.en: Leaf warblers, reed warblers and tree warblers in one quiz

intro.en:
Warblers are a test of patience. After four lessons you can tell a Chiffchaff from a Willow Warbler and you know what the Siberian birds look like, and how a Marsh Warbler sings. This week there is a long quiz with twenty questions, with birds from all of block 2, and a few gulls from block 1 to keep you honest.

Many questions here are sound questions or photo-and-sound questions: warblers are mostly identified by their voice. Listen first, then look. If you get a Reed Warbler and a Marsh Warbler wrong, go back to the song descriptions and play the recordings again.

A good result is fifteen right. Do not worry about the Siberian birds: they are rare, and many experienced birders still need a second look at a Yellow-browed Warbler.

outside.en: Go for a walk at dawn in May or at the coast in autumn. Write down every warbler you hear, with the key notes about its voice. Compare your list with a bird app or a friend.

next.en: Next block: waders. Dunlin, Little Stint, Curlew Sandpiper and other small waders.
